ALHAMBRA DESIGN REVIEW BOARD
  SPECIAL MEETING
  AGENDA
  111 South First Street
  June 9, 2020
  5:00 P.M.

  CORONAVIRUS (COVID-19) ADVISORY NOTICE
Consistent with Executive Orders No. N-29-20 and No. N-35-20 from the Executive Department of the
State of California and the County of Los Angeles Department of Public Health Safer At Home Order, the
Alhambra Design Review Board meeting will not be physically open to the public and the meeting will
take place via teleconference and video conference.

To watch and listen to the meeting: To maximize public safety while still maintaining transparency and
public access, members of the public can participate by using Zoom Meeting as follows:

Zoom Meeting direct link:
https://us02web.zoom.us/j/81146906696?pwd=ejlUWGdRQW5ERDBOcHM3WVBrOTBHdz09
Meeting ID: 811 4690 6696and Password: 399410

Or by telephone by dialing 1-669-900-6833, 1-253-215-8782, 1-346-248-7799, 1-312-626-6799, 1-929-
205-6099, or 1-301-715-8592 and entering Meeting ID: 811 4690 6696 and Password: 399410. Please
Note: All members of the public calling or logging into the meeting will be muted so that the meeting can
proceed.

For those wishing to speak on an agenda item, please email Erin Joson at eung@cityofalhambra.org no
later than 4:00 p.m. prior to the meeting with the item number you wish to speak on and the phone
number you will use when calling or the name you will use when logging into the meeting. You should
then call or log into the meeting at least 10 minutes prior to its start time. Staff will unmute you and
announce you when it is your time to speak. You will have five minutes to speak, unless that time is
adjusted by the Chairperson. If you do not have access to a computer please call 626-570-3256 to request
public comment.

As an alternative you can email your comments by sending them to the Design Review Board by email at
eung@cityofalhambra.org no later than 3:00 p.m. to ensure that Design Review Board Staff have time to
print the emails prior to the beginning of the meeting. Comments will then be read into the record, with
a maximum allowance of 5 minutes per individual comment, subject to the Chairperson’s discretion. If a
comment is received after 3:00 p.m. but before the beginning of the meeting based upon its time stamp,
the comment will still be included as a part of the record of the meeting but will not be read into the
record.

Any member of the public who needs accommodations or who needs their comments translated should
email or call the Community Development Department at plam@cityofalhambra.org or (626) 570-5034.
All requests for accommodations or translation services shall be made by 3:00 p.m. the Thursday prior to
the Design Review Board meeting. If accommodation or translation is not requested by 3:00 p.m. the
Thursday prior to the Design Review Board meeting, staff will try to accommodate the request to the best
of their efforts to provide as much accessibility as possible while also maintaining public safety. Given the
challenges of teleconference and videoconference meetings, all participants are encouraged to email
their comments prior to the beginning of the meeting.

CONSENT CALENDAR (Item 1):

All items listed under Consent Calendar are considered by the Design Review Board to be
routine and will be enacted by one motion unless a citizen or Board Member requests
otherwise; in which case, the item will be removed for separate consideration. Items
placed under Consent Calendar include smaller scale projects with no or minor design
issues and ministerial matters (minutes).

1.  MINUTES: April 14, 2020
Recommended Action: Design Review Board review and approve as submitted the
minutes of the April 14, 2020 special meeting of the Design Review Board.

DISCUSSION ITEMS:

2.  2990 & 2970 West Valley Boulevard
This is an application for a new car wash building
Applicant: Artem Golestian, Cenmill Inc.

Recommended Action: APPROVAL - Recommendation is for approval with the following
conditions: 1. All signage shall be addressed under separate application; however, the
concept of a debossed sign in the concrete on the primary elevation is supported; 2. The
details for the metal louvers shall be adequately documented to ensure appropriate
execution of the architectural intent; and 3. All revised drawings shall be reviewed and
approved by DRB staff prior to the Planning Commission review.

  2
 PUBLIC COMMENTS/ORAL COMMUNICATIONS:
Citizens wishing to address the Alhambra Design Review Board on any matter within the
subject matter jurisdiction of the Alhambra Design Review Board not on the Agenda may
do so at this time. Please STATE YOUR NAME AND ADDRESS CLEARLY for the record.

Please note that while the Alhambra Design Review Board values your comments, pursuant
to January 1, 1987 amendments of the Brown Act, the Commission cannot respond nor take
any action until such time as the matter may appear as an item on a forthcoming agenda.

ADJOURNMENT:

  NOTICE:
AGENDA ITEMS: Copies of the staff reports or other written documentation relating to each
item of business described hereinabove are on file in the offices of the Community
Development Department in City Hall, 111 South First Street, Alhambra, California, and are
available for public inspection during office hours, which are 7:00 a.m. to 12:00 noon.
Monday through Thursday. Should any person have a question concerning any of the above
agenda items prior to the meeting described herein, he or she may contact the Community
Development Department either in person at the Department offices, or by telephone at
(626) 570-5034 during regular office hours.

APPEALS: Any person wishing to appeal any decision of the Design Review Board to the
Planning Commission may do so by filing an appeal in writing along with the appropriate
appeal fee to the Community Development Department in City Hall within 10 calendar days
of the Design Review Board decision. The appeal period for items on this agenda expires at
the close of business on Monday, June 22, 2020.

  April 14, 2020, 4:30 p.m. via teleconference.

  Call to Order: At 4:32 p.m. on April 14, 2020, the Design Review Board convened
  via teleconference.

  Roll Call/Introductions

  PRESENT:  CHEN, CHIU, OLSON

ELECTION OF OFFICERS:

The Design Review Board shall hold an election for Board Member positions for Chairman,
Vice Chairman and Secretary.

Discussion:
Board Member Steven Chen nominated Christine Olson for Chairman. Board Member Katie
Chiu seconded. A vote was taken; all were in favor of Board Member Christine Olson for
Chairman. Board Member Christine Olson was elected for the Chairman position. Board
Member Katie Chiu nominated Steven Chen for Vice Chairman. A vote was taken; all were in
favor of Board Member Steven Chen for Vice Chairman. Board Member Steven Chen was
elected for the Vice Chairman position. Vice Chairman Steven Chen nominated Richard Abe
for Secretary. Chairman Christine Olson seconded. A vote was taken; all were in favor of
Richard Abe for Secretary. Richard Abe was elected for the Secretary position. Board
Members Christine Olson and Steven Chen ran the remainder of the meeting as President
and Vice-President, respectively.

ACTION:
The Design Review Board elected Chairman Christine Olson for Chairman, Board Member
Steven Chen for Vice Chairman and Richard Abe for Secretary.

CONSENT AGENDA (ITEM 1)

All items listed under Consent Agenda were considered by the Design Review Board to be
routine and, therefore, were enacted by one motion.

ITEM 1: 1237 East Main Street
  Request:
  The applicant, Superior Electrical Advertising, on behalf of Davita Kidney Care,
  Business Tenant, proposes new signage to an existing commercial building for a
  1
   business known as "Davita Kidney Care." The design consists of two lines of copy
  using internally illuminated channel letters for the upper line of copy and plastic
  surface mounted letters for the secondary line. The two new building signs are
  located at the south (front) and west elevations and are the same size. They use a
  design that is consistent with the recognized national brand which is blue in color.
  The other signs proposed are vinyl door signs for directional purposes. The main
  entrance door uses a white vinyl and the remaining directional vinyl signs are
  black. Sizes and designs are acceptable.

  ACTION
  Vice Chairman Chen moved to approve Consent Agenda Item 1. Board Member
  Chiu seconded and the motion carried.

  Vote:  Moved: CHEN  Seconded: CHIU
  Ayes: CHEN, CHIU, OLSON
  Abstain: NONE
  Noes: NONE
  Absent: UDANI

DISCUSSION ITEMS:

ITEM 2: 1903 South Meridian Avenue
  Request:
  The applicant Thang Nguyen, Property Owner, proposes to replace the existing
  backyard fence of an existing single-family residence. This property is located on a
  steep upslope through lot with the rear yard facing Grandview Drive. The existing
  rear fence is a rusted chainlink fence and will be replaced with a 5'-4" high
  horizontal plank white vinyl fence. The fence will also include a man gate where
  the existing stairs are located. Although the existing and proposed fences enclose
  the portion of the property that functions as the backyard, the through lot
  condition requires that this area be treated similar to a front yard and that any
  fencing is limited to a maximum height of 3’-0”. A Modification application for a
  taller fence has been submitted and is subject to review and approval by the
  Community Development Director. The proposed design is acceptable for the
  location of this fence.

  Project discussion was as follows:
  Thang Nguyen was present on the call to speak for this item. Board Member Chiu
  was accepting of the design. Vice Chairman Chen confirmed with the applicant
  that the side fences were chain link. Vice Chairman Chen questioned the extent of
  the fence and if the fences should match. The owner stated that the chain link
  fences extend all the way to the back. They are only proposing changing the rear
  fence. Vice Chairman Chen stated that he had no problem with the design. Vice
  Chairman Chen moved to approve the application with the condition that the
  approval is contingent upon approval of the Modification application by the

  2
   Community Development Director. Board Member Chiu seconded and the motion
  carried.

  ACTION
  The Design Review Board approved the application with the condition that the
  approval is contingent upon approval of the Modification application by the
  Community Development Director.

  Vote:  Moved: CHEN  Seconded: CHIU
  Ayes: CHEN, CHIU, OLSON
  Abstain: NONE
  Noes: NONE
  Absent: UDANI

ITEM 3: 3000 West Valley Boulevard
  Request:
  The applicant Ruby Goldenberg, on behalf of the Property Owner, proposes an
  amendment to a Uniform Sign Program for an existing multi-tenant commercial
  building. The amendment includes allowing options for both primary and
  secondary signs to have two lines of copy, allowing the option of a cloud detail for
  signs that need a raceway due to J-Box access issues, and the secondary signs be
  reverse channel letters with an option for illumination. Although there are various
  options added, since there are only two tenants in the building it may be
  acceptable. Consideration should be made to include a note that states each
  tenant's primary and secondary signs shall match. Locations of the signs shall be
  referred to the elevation drawings as the secondary sign of Tenant B is not
  centered on the tenants lease space on that elevation. Dimensions and/or notes
  shall be added on the elevations.

  Project discussion was as follows:
  Johnny Estrada, on behalf of the applicant Ruby Goldenberg was present on the
  call to speak for this item. Erin Joson stated that this is for a revision to an existing
  Uniform Sign Program. Chairman Olson questioned why the sign is not centered on
  the building face. The applicant stated that centering between the windows was
  acceptable. Discussion ensued with the recognition that the dimensional locations
  of the signs were not shown on the drawings. Staff comments included a
  recommended condition of approval. The applicant questioned how the conditions
  of approval were to be documented. Erin Joson explained the necessary
  documentation. Vice Chairman Chen moved to approve the application with the
  following conditions: 1) The Design Standards shall note that each tenant's primary
  and secondary signs shall be consistent in style; 2) The sign details shall refer to
  the elevation drawings for sign locations; 3) The elevation drawings shall include
  dimensions and/or notes for locations of each sign; and 4) The drawings shall be
  reviewed and approved by DRB staff prior to permit issuance. Board Member Chiu
  seconded and the motion carried.

  3
   ACTION
  The Design Review Board approved the application with the following conditions:
  1) The Design Standards shall note that each tenant's primary and secondary signs
  shall be consistent in style; 2) The sign details shall refer to the elevation drawings
  for sign locations; 3) The elevation drawings shall include dimensions and/or notes
  for locations of each sign; and 4) The drawings shall be reviewed and approved by
  DRB staff prior to permit issuance.

  Vote:  Moved: CHEN  Seconded: CHIU
  Ayes: CHEN, CHIU, OLSON
  Abstain: NONE
  Noes: NONE
  Absent: UDANI

ITEM 4: 1621 West Shorb Street
  Request:
  The applicant Dolores Aguilar, Property Owner, proposes to alter the fenestration
  of an existing single-family residence. A majority of the windows will be replaced,
  two new windows will be added at the southeast corner, and a patio door will be
  replaced. There are several details that are missing from the submitted drawings
  that should be addressed including existing window types and window details. The
  applicant is proposing both retrofit and nail-on windows and should confirm how
  the details will be treated for consistency.

  Project discussion was as follows:
  The applicant was not present. Board Member Chiu stated that she was in
  agreement with Staff comments. Windows number 5 and 6 should be two hung
  windows mulled together. Vice Chairman Chen concurred. Vice Chairman Chen
  moved to approve the application with the following conditions: 1) Hung windows
  shall be used throughout; 2) Windows 5 & 6 shall be two hung windows mulled
  together; 3) Window details shall be consistent throughout; 4) The bedroom patio
  door shall be specified as such; and 5) Revised drawings shall be reviewed and
  approved by DRB staff prior to permit issuance. Board Member Chiu seconded and
  the motion carried.

  ACTION
  The Design Review Board approved the application with the following conditions:
  1) Hung windows shall be used throughout; 2) Windows 5 & 6 shall be two hung
  windows mulled together; 3) Window details shall be consistent throughout; 4)
  The bedroom patio door shall be specified as such; and 5) Revised drawings shall
  be reviewed and approved by DRB staff prior to permit issuance.

  Vote:  Moved: CHEN  Seconded: CHIU
  Ayes: CHEN, CHIU, OLSON
  Abstain: NONE
  Noes: NONE
  Absent: UDANI
  4
 ITEM 5: 121 East Main Street
  Request:
  The applicant Vincent Huen, on behalf of Rev Watches, Business Tenant, proposes
  exterior alterations to an existing commercial building for the business known as
  "Rev Watches." Alterations consist of extending the entrance towards the street,
  adding a new frameless glass storefront system and restoring the existing metal
  canopy to accommodate a new sign. The proposed elevations show a sign that
  covers the front of the canopy, however, signage will be submitted under a
  separate application and should not be reviewed at this time. The new storefront
  system does not include a transom condition and will extend the header over the
  entrance area. Although the new color palette for this tenant space is acceptable,
  consideration and clarification should be made as to where the new paint starts
  and stops as it relates to the adjacent nail salon. Despite the fact that these two
  businesses are located on separate properties, the two spaces share an overall
  façade. Consideration should be made for using complimentary colors.

  Project discussion was as follows:
  Vincent Huen and Jay Zapata were present on the call to speak for this item. The
  applicant stated that they are just painting the portion of the building in between
  the columns. They are still maintaining the rest of the building materials and
  finishes. They are also increasing the size of the glazing. Chairman Olson
  commented on the existing color palette of the building. Vice Chairman Chen
  questioned if the proposed canopy is different than existing. There was discussion
  regarding the black rectangle on the front elevation. This is not included in this
  current application. It is tied to the signage design and will be addressed under
  separate application. There was confusion as to the painting of the building as it
  relates to the rest of the building. Vice Chairman Chen moved to approve the
  application with the following conditions: 1) The paint colors shall be restudied as
  it relates to the overall facade shared by the adjacent nail salon; 2) The applicant
  work with staff regarding the color palette specifications; and 3) Any revised colors
  shall be updated in the drawings and reviewed and approved by DRB staff prior to
  permit issuance. Board Member Chiu seconded and the motion carried.

  ACTION
  The Design Review Board approved the application with the following conditions:
  1) The paint colors shall be restudied as it relates to the overall facade shared by
  the adjacent nail salon; 2) The applicant work with Staff regarding the color palette
  specifications; and 3) Any revised colors shall be updated in the drawings and
  reviewed and approved by DRB staff prior to permit issuance.

  Vote:  Moved: CHEN  Seconded: CHIU
  Ayes: CHEN, CHIU, OLSON
  Abstain: NONE
  Noes: NONE
  Absent: UDANI

  5
 ITEM 6: 2499 West Main Street
  Request:
  The applicant John Jae Yong Chung, on behalf of GreenTree Inn & Suites, Business
  Tenant, proposes exterior alterations to an existing commercial building known as
  "GreenTree Inn & Suites." The alterations consist of repainting the building with a
  lighter more neutral color palette. Due to the inconsistent use of the paint colors
  throughout the building, the applicant should clarify their design intention. The
  rear elevation shows stonework being added to the first floor which should be
  noted on the drawings to match existing, if accurate. As with all projects with
  substantial exterior alterations, painting of the entire building is assumed.

  Project discussion was as follows:
  John Jae Yong Chung was present on the call to speak for this item. The applicant
  stated that there is no new stone planned. Vice Chairman Chen confirmed that
  there is no new signage. The metal railing will be repainted. Board Member Chiu
  stated that she accepted the proposal. Erin Joson clarified the Staff comment that
  there were blocks of different colors used rather than a consistent body color used
  throughout. Vice Chairman Chen moved to approve the application with the
  following conditions: 1) The drawings shall be corrected to address the stonework
  that is shown on the rear elevation; and 2) Revised drawings shall be reviewed and
  approved by DRB staff prior to permit issuance. Board Member Chiu seconded and
  the motion carried.

  ACTION
  The Design Review Board approved the application with the following conditions:
  1) The drawings shall be corrected to address the stonework that is shown on the
  rear elevation; and 2) Revised drawings shall be reviewed and approved by DRB
  staff prior to permit issuance.

  Vote:  Moved: CHEN  Seconded: CHIU
  Ayes: CHEN, CHIU, OLSON
  Abstain: NONE
  Noes: NONE
  Absent: UDANI

  6
 PUBLIC COMMENTS
  There were no public comments.

ADJOURNMENT:
  At 5:38 p.m., as there was no further business for the Board to transact, the Design
  Review Board adjourned the meeting with unanimous consent to the next special
  meeting to be held via teleconferencing on Tuesday, March 24, 2020, at 5:00 p.m.

PASSED, APPROVED AND ADOPTED this 9th day of June, 2020.

   Item  2

  ALHAMBRA DESIGN REVIEW BOARD
  STAFF REPORT
  June 9, 2020

ADDRESS: 2990 & 2970 West Valley Boulevard
APPLICANT: Artem Golestian, Cenmill Inc.
PROPERTY OWNER: Jaam Wash
PROJECT TYPE: This application is for a new car wash building
PROJECT STATUS: First Time Applicant

DESIGN ASSESSMENT: This application proposes a new car wash building at the southeast
corner of Valley Boulevard and Cabrillo Avenue. The street is commercial in use and the
building is appropriate in both mass and architectural style. The style is a contemporary
aesthetic with durable materials consistent with the approach (i.e. textured concrete,
metal panels and stucco in a neutral color palette). The metal louvers at the top of the
building provide a needed visual reveal that serves as a functional and aesthetic detail.
There is little detail given for the louvers including the number, attachment and backing to
the louvers. A clear understanding and documentation of the detail should be provided
prior to full entitlement.

The main sign proposed is integral to the architecture and should be addressed under this
application. The word “carwash” is shown debossed in the textured concrete. If these were
standard channel letters, the size and prominence would be of concern, however, given
the purposeful integration with the building and added advantage that there is no internal
lighting, this approach can be seen as positive. In general, all signage is stronger when
addressed as an integral part of the architecture. Approval for the primary sign should be
considered in concept but the details of the sign need to be defined (i.e. font, depth of
debossing and consistency with secondary signage). The details of the primary sign and all
secondary signage shown should be addressed under a separate application.

RECOMMENDATION: Recommendation is for approval with the following conditions: 1.
All signage shall be addressed under separate application; however, the concept of a
debossed sign in the concrete on the primary elevation is supported; 2. The details for the
metal louvers shall be adequately documented to ensure appropriate execution of the
architectural intent; and 3. All revised drawings shall be reviewed and approved by DRB
staff prior to the Planning Commission review.
